Marathon Petroleum stock rose 0.31% today to close at $388.90, extending a strong two-week rally of 7.81%. The gain reflects sustained strength in refining conditions: U.S. refineries are running at 98% capacity utilization, and diesel prices have hit record highs as Ukraine continues bombing Russian refineries and Russia restricts diesel exports. For a major U.S. refiner like Marathon, tight global diesel supply and full-capacity operations mean stronger margins on the fuel they produce.

The broader geopolitical backdrop is amplifying this. The recent Trump administration deal with Venezuela, combined with EU and South Korea escalating sanctions against Iran and threatening to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, creates supply uncertainties that support higher crude prices (Brent at $96, WTI at $91.48). Higher crude prices and constrained global refining capacity—especially with Russian refinery disruptions—push refined product prices higher and favor U.S. refiners operating at near-peak rates.
